chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskhan from Muhammad al-Halabi said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about al-Sawad (the fertile lands of Iraq), what is its status? He said: 'It belongs to all Muslims, for those who are here today, and for those who will enter Islam after today, and for those who have not yet been created.'

We said: The purchase is from the landowners (al-Dahakin). He said: 'It is not suitable except that he buys from them on the condition that he dedicates it to the Muslims. If the ruler (Wali al-Amr) wishes to take it, he takes it.'
We said: And if he takes it from him? He said: 'He returns to him the principal capital, and for him is what he consumed from its produce, according to what he worked.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on the ownership and purchase of al-Sawad lands?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* articulates the Shia juristic view of al-Sawad as a perpetual public endowment (waqf) for the entire Muslim ummah, transcending temporal boundaries. It details the mechanism of private ownership contingent upon dedication to the community, granting the Wali al-Amr the prerogative of expropriation (kharaj) with specific compensation rules that distinguish between capital repayment and labor-based produce retention.
